title: $\texttt{findr}$: Transparent and Fair Credit Risk Decisions through Semi-Structured Regressions
abstract: arXiv:2608.24582v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Credit risk models increasingly need to combine predictive accuracy with transparent explanations and auditable fairness constraints. Logistic regression remains attractive because its coefficients are easy to interpret, but it can miss nonlinear structure. Flexible models can improve prediction, but their explanations are often post-hoc and may not describe the decision rule itself. We introduce $\texttt{findr}$, short for flexible, interpretable deep regression, a semi-structured framework for binary credit risk modelling that decomposes the logit into an interpretable structured component and an orthogonal neural residual. The orthogonalisation separates coefficient-based effects from residual nonlinear variation, while an in-processing Wasserstein penalty mitigates group disparities by comparing score distributions during training. The framework also includes diagnostics that measure the structured component's contribution to logit

translated_title: $\texttt{findr}$：通过半结构化回归实现透明且公平的信用风险决策
translated_abstract: 信用风险模型日益需要在预测准确性与透明解释和可审计的公平性约束之间取得平衡。逻辑回归因其系数易于解释而具有吸引力，但它可能无法捕捉非线性结构。灵活模型可以改善预测，但其解释往往是事后性的，可能无法描述决策规则本身。我们引入了$\texttt{findr}$，即灵活可解释深度回归的简称，这是一种用于二元信用风险建模的半结构化框架，它将逻辑回归的对数几率分解为可解释的结构化组件和一个正交的神经残差。正交化将基于系数的影响与残差非线性变化分离，同时一种处理中的Wasserstein惩罚通过比较训练期间的分数分布来减轻群体差异。该框架还包括诊断方法，用于衡量结构化组件对对数几率的贡献。
tldr: 本文提出了一个半结构化信用风险建模框架，通过正交化分离可解释线性组件与神经残差，并嵌入Wasserstein公平性惩罚，实现透明、可审计且公平的决策。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a semi-structured credit risk modeling framework that separates interpretable linear components from neural residuals via orthogonalization, and incorporates a Wasserstein fairness penalty to achieve transparent, auditable, and fair decisions.
